newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia vows crackdown on opposition alliance.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia vows crackdown on opposition alliance.

text.p: Indonesia has cracked down on a growing alliance between supporters of a Moslem-based minority party and the ousted leader of a rival party ahead of the May 29 general elections, news reports said on Tuesday.

The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Interior Minister Yogie Memet as saying the display of banners and pictures suggesting any alliance between Megawati Sukarnoputri, the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), and the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) had been banned.
"I declare that people are not to use those banners. We don't recognise any party but the three poll contestants," Memet, who is also chairman of the general election committee, was quoted as saying.
Supporters of Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, have been attending rallies of the PPP carrying her pictures and banners depicting an alliance between the two.

Megawati was removed as PDI chief by a government-backed faction last year and has been barred from the elections. She had asked her supporters not to take part in the campaign but appears to have tacitly approved the link-up with the PPP.
The PPP and the PDI are battling the ruling Golkar party for 425 elected seats in the 500-member parliament. The rest of the seats are allocated for the military, whose members do not vote.
The government-backed faction of the PDI appears to be doing badly in the campaign and could be routed in the polls, political analysts have said.

They have said that the alliance between Megawati supporters and the PPP is perhaps the only interesting feature of an otherwise lacklustre campaign but stressed that it would have little effect on Golkar's forecast easy win.
Memet said the banners breached election rules and an agreement among the three parties contesting the general elections. The Jakarta Post gave no further details.

The Post quoted Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, Armed Forces Chief of Socio-Political Affairs, as telling reporters that security forces would seize banners or T-shirts and ban chants in support of the "Mega-Bintang" (star) alliance.
The star is the PPP's symbol and banners and flags emblazoned "Mega-Bintang" have been waved at many PPP rallies.
"I call on them (Megawati supporters) not to display the outlawed banners at the next rally," Hamid said without elaborating.
The PPP is next scheduled to campaign on Wednesday in Jakarta where signs of the alliance have been most visible.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
